description: Historical festival archive. Entries distinguish permanent discontinuation, edition-specific endings, indefinite hiatuses and cancelled projects. The archive is separate from the active 2027 directory.

festivals.name: Love Parade
festivals.organizer: Love Parade GmbH / Lopavent (historical organizers; changed over time)
festivals.venue: Various locations: Berlin (1989–2006); Ruhr area (2007–2010). Final edition: former freight station, Duisburg.
festivals.reasonEnded: After the mass-casualty disaster at the Duisburg edition on 24 July 2010, the organizer announced that the Love Parade would not continue. 21 people died and hundreds were injured. The 2009 Bochum edition had already been cancelled for safety concerns.
festivals.notes: The event began on Berlin's Kurfürstendamm in 1989 with about 150 participants. It moved from Berlin to the Ruhr area in 2007. This archive record describes the historical Love Parade series; later techno parades such as Rave the Planet are not treated as the same active festival entry.

festivals.name: T in the Park
festivals.reasonEnded: The festival announced a break after 2016. The move from Balado to Strathallan in 2015 brought significant planning, site-layout, transport and operational constraints; the organizer said the restrictions made the expected festival experience unworkable.
festivals.notes: Official festival statement explains the move and site restrictions and says the event needed to take a year out. No later editions followed; last edition was 2016.

festivals.name: GlobalGathering UK
festivals.reasonEnded: The UK edition was put on hiatus for review after the 2014 event and did not return in 2015. Treat this as the end of the UK edition, not necessarily every international use of the GlobalGathering brand.
festivals.notes: UK edition only. International editions/brand history must be researched separately.

festivals.name: Big Day Out
festivals.city: Touring festival across Australia and New Zealand
festivals.venue: Multiple city venues; final 2014 tour included Perth, Adelaide, Gold Coast, Sydney, Melbourne and Auckland
festivals.reasonEnded: The 2015 edition was cancelled after ownership changed to C3 Presents. Promoters cited financial and operational challenges; the planned revival did not materialize.
festivals.notes: Map pin represents Sydney as a reference location for a multi-city touring festival; the archive entry documents the overall series, not a single fixed venue.

festivals.name: Sonisphere Festival – UK
festivals.reasonEnded: The UK edition did not return after 2014. The promoter later said the financial risk and rising costs of staging a large-scale UK festival made the model unviable. The wider Sonisphere brand continued to be used in other territories.
festivals.notes: UK edition only. Do not classify the international Sonisphere brand as globally discontinued.

festivals.name: Woodstock 50
festivals.city: Watkins Glen / Merriweather Post Pavilion (planned sites)
festivals.venue: Originally Watkins Glen International; later proposed Merriweather Post Pavilion. Festival never took place.
festivals.reasonEnded: The 50th-anniversary festival was cancelled after a series of setbacks involving permits, financing and production. No public festival edition took place.
festivals.notes: This is a cancelled planned anniversary event, not a festival series that ran and then ended. Kept in the archive as a notable cancelled festival project.

festivals.name: Falls Festival
festivals.city: Multi-site: Lorne, Marion Bay, Byron Bay, Fremantle and others
festivals.venue: Multiple sites; final season 2022/23 across Byron Bay, Fremantle and Melbourne
festivals.reasonEnded: The organizers announced a break after the 2022/23 season to rest, recover and reconsider the festival's future. This is recorded as an indefinite hiatus, not a confirmed permanent closure.
festivals.notes: A hiatus entry, not marked permanently discontinued. Marion Bay location ended earlier than the wider Falls Festival brand.

festivals.name: Splendour in the Grass
festivals.reasonEnded: The 2024 edition was cancelled and organizers subsequently announced that the festival would not return in 2025, describing the pause as time to recharge. The promoter retained support for a possible future return, so it is not classified as permanently discontinued.
festivals.notes: Indefinite hiatus; do not call permanently ended unless organizers make that explicit.
